concepts.def: Ricardo (1817): countries gain by specialising in goods of lowest opportunity cost, then trading.
Index of export prices / index of import prices x 100; improving means more imports per unit exported.
Viner (1950): customs unions create trade with members but divert trade from cheaper non-members.
World Trade Organization (1995, successor to GATT); 164 members; oversees trade agreements and dispute settlement.
Tax on imports; raises domestic prices; creates deadweight loss and may invite retaliation.
Quotas, technical standards, subsidies, anti-dumping duties; harder to measure than tariffs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The National and International Economy — a core area of A-Level Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The National and International Economy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The National and International Economy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
